html:
Tasks and recipes

A durable task persists a goal, status, attempts and checkpoints across API requests. route_groups/task_service.py owns task lifecycle and current-run projection. route_groups/tasks.py exposes task routes. Task execution re-enters the normal model-led runtime.

Follow durable task dispatch and lifecycle projections for generic task acceptance, queue capacity, failed submission reconciliation, monitoring, cancellation and deletion sequences.

Composer submissions use the server-owned coordinator in route_groups/conversation_tasks.py. Accepted tasks retain their selected model and execution profile/map while queued; dispatch resolves Recommended for the actual selected model. The running task then pins the resolved configuration and output reservation. Resume and Continue task retain that inference identity even if global settings change. Start a new task to use a changed Model Configuration.

Closing the browser tab does not stop accepted queued work while the server is running. Dependencies, available capacity and required user responses still control progress. See top-level task scheduling.

Task lifetime includes its queue, waits and verified continuations. Its timing projection uses all attempts and compact receipts, independently of visible history pagination; missing coverage remains unmeasured. See durable task and request timing for attribution, caching and recovery ownership.

Task storage and queue ownership

AgentTaskStore is the common constructor. An explicit hub, or a path already owned by the controller hub, selects the shared MemoryTaskStore. An unowned path uses the standalone SQLite implementation. The facade rejects a mismatched hub repository path. SQL initialization accepts the current schema version before repairing dependency projections; it does not infer edges by migrating unsupported historical schemas. See state publication and persistence for the controller's RAM authority and checkpoint lifecycle.

The records have separate responsibilities:

Record Responsibility
Task Accepted goal/context, logical identity, immutable creation sequence, explicit dependencies and progress projection
Attempt One request's trigger, parent request, status and bounded outcome previews
Checkpoint A task activity summary, deduplicated by task, request and trace-event identity
Lane Conversation queue order and a revision used to reject stale edits
Submission The client submission ID, accepted digest and task identity, retained to prevent replay
Request binding The committed request-to-task/attempt/lane identity used before dispatch and during recovery

Native execution state remains owned by RunStore. A task status, checkpoint or queue projection is not proof that an external command has stopped or succeeded. Generic create_attempt inserts task history; conversation dispatch uses reserve_chat_attempt to validate and commit its binding before a worker starts.

ConversationTaskLanes implements the standalone SQL transactions; the RAM repository supplies corresponding operations through MemoryLanes. The queue coordinator owns dispatch and reconciliation. The SQL acceptance path can join composer and admission callbacks in one attached-store writer transaction. An admission failure rolls back task, lane and submission changes together. Matching submission retries reuse the accepted task; a changed digest conflicts, and a retained identity cannot recreate deleted task history. A conversation accepts at most 32 queued tasks.

flowchart LR A[Accepted submission] --> B[Task and submission identity] B --> C[Dependency and capacity eligibility] C --> D[Committed attempt and request binding] D --> E[Native execution owner] E --> F[Reconciliation and task projection] F --> C

Only never-started queued intent is editable. Prompt or parameter-snapshot changes invalidate prepared compiler output; reordering changes queue positions without rebinding dependency targets or immutable creation order. Reorder requests must include every future task exactly once and carry the current lane revision. Removing or clearing future work cancels and archives intent while retaining its submission identity. Queued preparation describes the separate compiler record and reservation fence.

Selection takes the first eligible future task per conversation. A failed or waiting prerequisite blocks its dependents; independent tasks can proceed. A newly unblocked older task regains its queue priority. Fully parallel Agent tasks use isolated journals and do not hold the shared conversation gate while waiting; Conversation/Ask tasks retain the shared-transcript constraint. These checks do not reserve physical resources or model slots. Reservation rechecks dependencies, capacity, runtime admission and preparation readiness. The authoritative scheduling policy is documented in top-level task scheduling.

Retry and continuation retain the logical task identity and creation sequence. Replacement attempts must name the accepted latest parent; explicit compiler retry can instead reopen its existing request and attempt. Native admission separately checks whether execution has settled. Explicit start/skip decisions retain the dependency edges and record a waiver plus a checkpoint. Stop/skip advancement revalidates the chosen next task and lane revision together with native ownership, pending work and continuation state. Stop with a requested summary defers dependency release until native finalization; the durable decision lets reconciliation finish after a crash.

History limits are pruning targets, not unconditional row caps. Referenced predecessors, pending amendments, unresolved chat work and protected follow-ups can keep older records alive. Ordinary task deletion removes task-owned attempts and checkpoints after these guards; it does not delete native execution history or clean up task scratch on its own. Conversation management coordinates those owners and preserves submission/request tombstones. Abandonment archives unresolved intent while preserving started execution evidence and uncertainty about external effects. See conversation lifecycle for management, abandonment and deletion ownership.

SQL dependency tests and RAM task tests cover acceptance rollback, concurrent deduplication, explicit edges, recovery and retention. Lane lifecycle tests check that terminal outcomes do not create implicit queue-wide gates.

Run-local plans and saved recipes

The optional manage_tasks board belongs to one run and contains high-level outcomes, dependencies, active task, notes and observed result/job references. The model may revise it as evidence changes. The board is a strategy aid; it is not executable code or a separate completion contract.

Recipes persist a reviewed intent and parameters. Each invocation starts fresh execution against current state. A saved recipe does not silently replay old commands or promote old observations to current evidence.

See Workflow definitions, invocation and recovery for current saved-request ownership, revision pinning, context copies and retained recorded-workflow constraints.
